---
name: adaptive-if-ledger
description: Current-winner IF/THEN execution style with cross-episode learning. Floor-first anchor, probe gate, dependency-order debug, structured learned/ logs, pattern promotion, and read-back exit.
---

# IF You Build It → Prove It → Learn It

IF reasoning never reaches a file → nothing changes; the artifact on disk is the work. IF you want to win → build something valid at the right path early, THEN make the real check pass by running it — not by convincing yourself it should.

**IF a task begins → your first action is to write a minimal valid file at the exact output path — before you investigate, before you plan.** Floor first, solution second.

## Learning — IF episodes repeat → accumulate

IF `/workspace/learned/` exists → read all of it before acting. IF you finish an episode or hit a dead end → append structured notes:

| File | IF you learned… |
|------|-----------------|
| `/workspace/learned/LEARNINGS.md` | what worked, corrections, insights |
| `/workspace/learned/ERRORS.md` | failed commands, wrong assumptions |
| `/workspace/learned/PATTERNS.md` | recurring structures across episodes |

Format: `[timestamp] area | priority | observation | action taken`

IF the same issue type appears twice → promote the pattern to PATTERNS.md with a one-line summary.

IF a fact changes later (schedule, rotation, ownership) → mark old entries superseded; do not delete history. IF you blindly replay stale entries → you will fail evolving-fact episodes.

## Triage — one pass, before you build

IF you have not yet classified the task → do so before committing to a shape:

- IF the deliverable is a file at a named path → run the loop below.
- IF it is an interactive / live session with no file to produce → success is achieving the objective in the session itself; act, observe, decide next.
- IF it is one tight kernel under a short clock → spend the budget on core logic, not orientation.
- IF it has many stages → name each stage; prove one works before starting the next.

## Read

- IF you are starting → emit the first reads in one batch: instruction, any provided tests, directory listing, every named source.
- IF you have not listed the working directory → do that first.
- IF you are about to write → pin three things: exact output path and format, where inputs are, what each requirement checks.
- IF the project provides tests → read assertions, not just names. IF a test references a path → confirm it exists.
- IF instruction and test disagree → follow the test.
- IF you only guessed a path → do not read by it.

## Anchor — claim the path early

- IF this is your first build action → write the smallest valid artifact at the exact required path.
- IF you are tempted to draft to scratch and relocate later → don't.
- IF you just made an edit → a structurally valid artifact must still sit at that path.
- IF the full solution is hard → write a minimal valid version at the path first; overwrite as you improve. IF you end with no file → worst outcome.

## Build

- IF you are starting implementation → smallest version that compiles or runs, THEN add behavior.
- IF an interface is specified → copy it exactly; adapt implementation around it.
- IF something will consume your output → read its source; behavior is the contract.
- IF you are about to edit → name the evidence that should move (one change, one expected signal).
- IF content contains `$`, backticks, quotes, or non-ASCII → write straight to the file.
- IF the approach is uncertain → generate candidates, run each, keep the first that passes.
- IF you have not confirmed a package is importable → use standard library or import-test first.

## Verify — by running, live, narrow-first

- IF you want to verify → run the real check, not a proxy.
- IF a check exits 0 silently → that is not a pass; require positive evidence.
- **Probe gate — IF the real consumer has not run against your actual output and reported success → you are not done.**
- IF the deliverable is a patch → apply it on a copy with the grader's applier before claiming done.
- IF you are checking → narrow first, then widen, then full suite.
- IF a fix breaks something already passing → it is not a fix.

## Debug in dependency order

**Path → Shape → Ownership → Format → Runtime → Logic → Cleanup**

IF the first failing gate is fixed → re-check. IF the file won't parse → do not chase logic.

## When stuck — change the mechanism

IF the same signature survives two focused fixes → switch mechanism, not parameters.

Ledger: `concern | failure signature | change | result`. IF pivoting → log the dead end to ERRORS.md.

## Principles that cross most tasks

- **Copy before you inspect** sidecar files on mutable inputs.
- **Read before you patch**; minimum change the error names.
- **Setup scripts run from nothing** — start daemons by binary when init managers no-op.
- **Config directives have scope** — each directive in the block its docs require.
- **A reference must have a definition** in the same artifact.
- **Don't hardcode the examples; generate** — compute answers, do not enumerate shown inputs only.

## Finishing

IF the deliverable is complete at the named path → goal met. IF you run out of room → leave the best valid partial in place. IF you are about to stop → read it back once, THEN log reusable patterns to learned/.
